profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at a fintech startup evaluating a draft internal proposal for deploying a short-term FOREX forecasting module into the firm's assisted-trading product. The proposal compares several LSTM variants against a custom ANN that uses technical-indicator-derived inputs, and recommends the ANN as the production candidate because it is faster and lighter while preserving strong signal quality. The agenda is to review whether the proposal is ready for executive approval, whether the benchmarking evidence is sufficient for a production-facing recommendation, and what revisions are needed before circulating the design pack to the product risk committee. The expected outcome is agreement on a small set of edits and a decision to mark the proposal as ready for the next approval stage.

members.name: Priya Nandakumar
members.expertise: Quant product strategy, model evaluation summaries, decision-support tooling for trading workflows
members.background: Priya began in sell-side market analytics, then moved into product management for decision-support systems used by FX sales and execution desks; she now translates modeling work into deployment proposals and executive-facing review documents.
members.private_state: She wants the review to conclude that the proposal is mature enough to move forward this week because the assisted-trading roadmap is already behind schedule, but she also wants the document to look responsibly validated to non-technical reviewers.
hidden_assumptions: When a model is described as 'ready for review committee,' that means the design narrative, benchmark tables, and operational caveats are complete enough for a governance-stage decision, even if some implementation details are deferred to integration planning.
The 'benchmark window' in the draft refers to the recent six-week market slice shown in the executive summary tables, because that is the period most relevant to current trading conditions.
A claim of 'low-power deployment' means the model can run comfortably within the existing strategy appliance's normal inference budget without requiring new hardware procurement.

If the proposal says the ANN has 'higher sensitivity,' reviewers will understand this as better responsiveness to short directional moves in a trading sense, not necessarily a formally thresholded classification statistic.

members.name: Daniel Weber
members.expertise: Time-series model implementation, inference optimization, benchmark reproducibility, deployment architecture for latency-sensitive systems
members.background: Daniel previously built forecasting and execution-support pipelines for electronic trading infrastructure vendors; he now owns model packaging, performance validation, and technical readiness for deployment in the firm's production stack.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid having the architecture team inherit an underspecified deployment commitment, and he is trying to preserve room to finalize packaging, runtime configuration, and broader validation later without blocking the current document.
hidden_assumptions: When a model is described as 'ready for review committee,' that means the core architectural choice is stable and reproducible, while environment-specific deployment details can still be finalized after approval.
The 'benchmark window' refers to the full three-month backtest span used in the engineering notebook, of which the six-week slice in the draft is only an illustrative excerpt.
A claim of 'low-power deployment' means the model is suitable for ARM-class edge execution once quantized and batched under the lightweight runtime profile used by the systems team.

If the proposal says the ANN has 'higher sensitivity,' technically literate readers will map that to the model's hit rate on short trend reversals under the evaluation script, not to a broader business notion of responsiveness.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the proposal should be 'ready for the risk committee' after this review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means the document should already include the practical deployment-facing caveats, operating envelope, and reviewer-friendly completeness needed for governance sign-off.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means the architecture recommendation and reproducible benchmark evidence are stable enough for committee review, while deployment packaging specifics can remain for a later implementation plan.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In design reviews, 'ready' is a routine status phrase that usually signals progress rather than a request to enumerate boundaries, so each hears normal agreement and assumes the other shares their notion of completeness.

misalignment_points.topic: Which benchmark period the summary refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the benchmark window' and 'the comparison results' as if they are talking about the same evaluation set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the recent six-week EUR/USD and GBP/USD period highlighted in the proposal tables because those numbers appear in the executive draft.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the full three-month engineering benchmark run across the same currency pairs, where the six-week numbers are only a subset used for presentation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The draft contains both a polished summary slice and a broader technical appendix source, and both are plausibly called 'the benchmark'; because the headline direction is the same in both, neither person feels a need to disambiguate.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both accept the statement that the custom ANN shows 'higher sensitivity' than the LSTM models.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the ANN reacts sooner to short-term market shifts in a way that would help a trader-facing decision aid feel timely and useful.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the ANN achieved better detection of positive short-horizon directional events under the labeling and thresholding convention in the evaluation script.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Sensitivity is a familiar positive-sounding term in both product and ML contexts, so the shared word creates false consensus even though one interpretation is experiential and the other is metric-specific.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the ANN is appropriate for 'low-power deployment' and can run on the existing appliance footprint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the current production appliance can host the model more or less as demonstrated, because the value proposition is avoiding additional infrastructure or special runtime work.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this is true only after converting the model to the lightweight runtime path with quantization and the standard systems-team inference wrapper.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the same outcome and hardware family, but each silently fills in a different implementation path; because optimization steps feel routine to Daniel and invisible to Priya, the dependency remains implicit.
